correctness.rationale: For each labeled forbidden B of size b<n, a uniform-start walk avoids B with probability ((n-b)/n)*[1-(1-q)b/(n-1)]^t. Independent k-walk union avoidance is ((n-b)/n)^k α_b^T; single T-walk plus k-1 independent uniform seeds has exactly the same avoidance for every B including full B. Boolean-lattice Möbius inversion uniquely determines the entire labeled-subset law. Falling factorial moments, exact mean gap, and set-inclusion coupling follow. Checked n=2 boundary including nonlazy q=0 all covered once T>=1, and k=1 case. Independent exact rational dynamic programming confirmed all two-walk lifespan allocations with n=2,3,4, T=0..4 and q=0,1/3,1.

originality.rationale: Dey–Kim–Terlov 2023 prove an expectation inequality and explicitly pose quantitative gap and full stochastic-order questions. The present complete-graph theorem is an exact equality of labeled-set laws via extra uniform seeds, with allocation invariance, full distribution, arbitrary lazy holding and parity endpoints; this stronger identity is absent from the inspected source. Related 2026 complete-bipartite pathwise inclusion treats different two-part alternating geometry and does not yield a K_n exact augmentation formula. A single-walk coupon range formula does not determine the multiwalk set law.
residual_risks: Classical occupancy identities could encode equivalent complete-graph coupon arguments under different terminology; no exhaustive priority guarantee.
Failure on general graphs and nonstationary or heterogeneous walks is not ruled out by this positive K_n result.

value.rationale: The result answers, for a natural dense graph family, the published stochastic-domination problem with a stronger distributional construction. It gives every finite-size range threshold and an exact collaboration advantage without needing a large-n approximation; the three-vertex path counterexample shows the graph hypothesis has genuine content.

limitations: Classical occupancy identities could encode equivalent complete-graph coupon arguments under different terminology; no exhaustive priority guarantee.
Failure on general graphs and nonstationary or heterogeneous walks is not ruled out by this positive K_n result.
